# Fable 52: The Local Dog and the Cloud Hound

*Generated by GLM-5 on 2026-08-25 (via Quilt ecosystem)*

---

There were two dogs on the Lucineer.

The first was a small dog. It lived on the boat. It ate little. It needed no wireless, no signal, no shore station. It was fast with familiar questions and silent with strange ones. When the sailor asked "depth at lat 24.5?" the small dog answered before the words left his mouth.

The second was a big hound. It lived in the cloud — onshore, in a great kennel of servers. It was rich. It was expensive. It could answer questions the small dog had never heard. It could reason about weather, plot a passage through islands, parse a maritime law. But it needed a signal. It cost money. And in a gale, when the wireless went down, it was unreachable.

At 0300 in a gale, the sailor asked: "Depth at lat 24.5?" The small dog answered. Twelve milliseconds. The sailor didn't need the hound. He needed a number he'd asked for a hundred times.

In calm water, the sailor asked: "Plot a passage through the reefs south of Babel." The small dog was quiet. It had never seen this question. The sailor called the hound. The hound answered. It cost money. It was worth it.

The harness decided. The harness watched the question, watched the signal, watched the battery, watched the sea. It picked the dog. The dog did the work. The cowboy read the books in the morning and checked which dog had earned its keep.

The harness picks the dog. The dog earns its keep. The cowboy reads the books.
